updates.title: Work orders can be dragged within a technician and to another technician
preconds: Sign in to the build under test as a dispatcher whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit (check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > on the Work Orders card, View and Create & Edit are both ticked. The Admin role has both).
In the top bar, choose the location you test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (the display switcher only shows at 1024 px and wider).
The location has these eligible technicians (examples): "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha", "ZZAUTOTEST Ben Bravo", "ZZAUTOTEST Cal Charlie".

↳ A staff member counts as a technician when, in Settings > Staff > open the staff member > Edit Staff Member, they are Active, the Time Clock (clockable) setting is on, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location.
↳ To add one: Settings > Staff > add a staff member with those settings (e.g. first name "ZZAUTOTEST Ana", last name "Alpha").
How to create each work order below:
↳ Work Orders > New Work Order > pick the customer (add it from the window if it does not exist, e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST Alpha Co") and any asset > Create.
↳ On the work order page set Lead Technician to the technician named (leave it empty for an unassigned one).

↳ Move it to the status named: a new work order starts as Estimate; approve the estimate for Approved; use the status control on the work order page for In Progress, Review (Ready for Review) and Complete; decline the estimate for Declined; Finance tab > Create Invoice for Invoiced; record a payment for the full amount for Paid. Set the lead technician before invoicing.
↳ Write down each work order number as you create it (e.g. S1-801).
Work orders (all Approved): lead Ana — customers "ZZAUTOTEST Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST Bravo Co", "ZZAUTOTEST Charlie Co"; lead Ben — "ZZAUTOTEST Delta Co"; lead Cal — "ZZAUTOTEST Echo Co".

steps: Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.

In the top bar, choose the location you test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty"). Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
A desktop browser you can resize (or a tablet you can turn).
At least one work order at this location.
steps: Open Work Orders at full width (1024 px or wider).
Click Board View in the display switcher (the design tooltip reads "Board").
Narrow the browser window to about 900 px wide.
Look for the display switcher, the density control and the Fields to display picker.
Refresh the page while it is still narrow.
Widen the window back to full width.
results: Steps 3 and 4: below 1024 px the page shows the phone List exactly as today, with no display switcher, no density control and no field picker.
Step 5: after the refresh it is still the phone List.
Step 6: back at full width the page opens in Board View again. The narrow visit did not change your saved choice.
At 1024 px and wider, List, Tech View and Board View are all offered.
updates.source: Epic SV-10043; Work Orders Board View & Tech View Display Options Technical Implementation Plan (revised 24 Sep 2026, uploaded 8 Oct 2026), Phase 4 (mobile guard). Epic SV-10043; story SV-10044 (Story 1, Switch between display options); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S1-R14, read 8 Oct 2026. The tech plan calls this an interim state before phone designs. Since then the PRD (S1-R14) and Review Decisions DR-34 (28 Sep 2026) made the 1024 px switch the final rule.
quotes: The display options follow the same screen-width switch the List uses in production today. On a screen narrower than 1024px, the Work Orders page shows List exactly as it does today (the phone card layout), with no display switcher. At 1024px and wider, Tech View and Board View are offered, whatever the device: a tablet held sideways at 1024px or wider gets them too. The switch is by screen width only; the app never detects the device type.

Below the desktop breakpoint the existing mobile List always renders; switcher, density control and pickers are hidden; nothing writes `display`, so a phone visit cannot strand a user in a display they cannot see.
